Umbrella of skeletal dysplasias affecting distal limb development; endocrine and visceral abnormalities are subtype-specific.
Marrow failure/thrombocytopenia and radioulnar skeletal abnormalities define the variable syndrome; other organ abnormalities lack evidence of common involvement.
Sensorineural deafness and gonadal endocrine failure define Perrault syndrome; neuropathy and intellectual disability occurred in 2/2, cerebellar atrophy in 1/2.
The named syndrome combines congenital focal hair loss with abnormal brain enlargement; no evidence supports additional axes.
Hereditary coagulation factor defect causing a bleeding tendency; no additional organ disease is established.
Permanent universal alopecia, intellectual disability/epilepsy and destructive periodontal disease define the syndrome; hearing impairment is occasional.
Mesomelic skeletal dysplasia, digital malformations and intellectual disability define the syndrome.

Congenital keratinizing epithelial lesion of the ear that can erode middle-ear structures and impair hearing.
Valine metabolic defect with progressive neurodegeneration; strabismus and vertebral malformations each frequent (30-79%); isolated cardiac report does not establish common involvement.

Impaired cerebral face recognition without a vision disorder; no ocular damage is implied.
Hereditary motor neuron/peripheral nerve disease; denervation with thenar, interosseous and distal muscle atrophy is frequent (30-79%).
Isolated congenital duplication of the preaxial toe skeleton.
Primary neoplasm originating in the heart; embolic injury to other organs is not consistently present across this tumour umbrella.
Immune-mediated granulomatous disease with defining hypercalcemia; pulmonary involvement occurs in about 90%; renal stones and other separately coded complications excluded.
Inherited macular retinal dystrophy with reduced visual acuity in 8/8 patients.
Acquired selective erythroid marrow failure; primary adult PRCA is typically immune-mediated. Anemia-related dyspnea does not establish lung disease.
Congenital intrahepatic vascular malformation connecting hepatic arterial and portal venous circulations.
Malignant mesenchymal tumour originating in the urinary bladder, which belongs to the renal axis.
Early-onset hereditary parkinsonism with intellectual disability in 4/4 patients; psychiatric symptoms do not add an organ axis.
